proof.criterion: A failed install ends the start wrapper where it stands: the deployment's setup command never runs and Oh My Pi never starts on a plugin pair that was not installed.
proof.surface: TestAFailingInstallNeverRunsTheSetupCommandOrTheAgent in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox, running the rendered wrapper through the package's own runStart harness with a stand-in bun that exits non-zero, a stand-in node, and recorder stand-ins for the setup command and the agent.
proof.observed: Both subtests pass: the failing case exits 1, writes the install's own `legion plugins: installing @sjawhar/pi-legion@9.7.0 and @sjawhar/pi-envoy@9.6.1 failed` to stderr, leaves stdout — the shim's frame stream — empty, and neither the setup log nor the agent log exists; the succeeding case exits 0 with both logs present.
proof.negativeControl: The succeeding case is the control and runs in the same test: without it the failing case's absent markers would prove only that the harness ran nothing at all.

proof.criterion: The new test fails when the behaviour it pins is removed — checked in that order, before the test was trusted.
proof.surface: installBlock's rendered failure branch in plugins.go.
proof.command: the rendered `|| { echo %s; exit 1; }` changed to `|| { echo %s; }`, then `go test -count=1 -run TestAFailingInstallNeverRuns ./internal/runtime/sandbox/`, then restored
proof.observed: FAIL, three lines: `the wrapper exited 0, want 1`, `the setup command ran after a failed install (<nil>): the install's subshell exit did not end the wrapper`, and the same for the agent. Restored: `ok … 0.076s`, plugins.go back to checksum 741d9ee605423d52.
proof.negativeControl: The restore is the control for the mutation: the same command on the unmutated render passes, so the failure is the deleted branch's and not the harness's.

proof.criterion: The merged tree is otherwise unchanged by this round.
proof.surface: The whole sandbox package at the new head.
proof.command: gofmt -l ./internal; go vet ./internal/runtime/sandbox/; go test -count=1 ./internal/runtime/sandbox/; jj diff --stat
proof.observed: gofmt clean, vet ok, `ok … 140.663s`, and the round's diff is one file, `plugins_test.go`, +56/−0 — no production code and no prose, so the branch's diff against its base is where the merge left it.
proof.negativeControl: The diff stat is the control for that claim: a round that had touched the render or the documentation would show it there.

filesChanged: packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins_test.go — TestAFailingInstallNeverRunsTheSetupCommandOrTheAgent, the install-side mirror of main's TestAFailingSetupCommandNeverStartsTheAgent, with the succeeding case as its control in the same test.
trickyParts: The install's failure is the one in this wrapper that crosses a subshell boundary: installBlock renders `( … ) 1>&2`, so a failed `bun add` exits the subshell and only `set -e` in the wrapper makes it the wrapper's own exit. That is why the mutation deletes the `exit 1` rather than the message, and why the test asserts the wrapper's exit and the two absent logs rather than the stderr line alone.
deviations: The commit carrying this test, 0e21bab7d988, is authored by the reviewer's App rather than mine: the working-copy commit this turn started on was the reviewer's, in the workspace all roles share, and I split it before reading its author. The handoff commit above it is mine. I did not rewrite the pushed commit to correct the attribution — rewriting a pushed commit for authorship alone is not one of the sanctioned rewrites, and a code commit's author reaches no gate — so it is recorded here instead.
discoveredComplexity: Absent evidence again, in its narrowest form: the tester's live run showed the failure propagating, and nothing in the suite would have noticed if it stopped. A behaviour proven once by hand on freshly restructured code is not a behaviour that is held.
